def add_members
    group = Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)
    usernames = params.require(:usernames)

    return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic

    existing_user_ids = group.user_ids

    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      usernames.split(",").each do |username|
        if user = User.find_by_username(username)
          next if existing_user_ids.include?(user.id)
          group.add(user)

  end

result.oneSentenceSummary: close() joins commit thread before draining workers, losing final offsets
result.improvedCode:
def close(self) -> None:
        self.shutdown_event.set()
        self.queue_pool.shutdown()
        self.commit_thread.join(timeout=5.0)
        committable = self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.get_committable_offsets()
        if committable:
            metrics.incr(
                "remote_subscriptions.queue_pool.offsets_committed",
                len(committable),
                tags={"identifier": self.queue_pool.identifier},
            )
            self.commit_function(committable)
            for partition, offset in committable.items():
                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.mark_committed(partition, offset)

judge.titleReason: The title names the defect: close() joins the commit thread before workers are drained, so the final offsets are lost.
judge.fixReason: The reference says the fix needs a wider change: queue_pool.shutdown() sets the worker stop flags before draining their queues, so queued work can still be dropped, and this edit does not change the pool; the final commit also runs with no exception handling or serialization guarantees beyond the join timeout.
